policy_note: Not the same check as no-std-policy.json's larql-core row. That one asks 'is the whole crate no_std yet' (currently no, missing the crate-root opt-out). This one asks a narrower, diagnostic question: with `io` (std::fs-coupled) and `engine` (network-coupled via the `http` feature) both switched off via `--no-default-features`, does the remaining `algo`+`core` surface -- the pure graph algorithms and their Graph/Edge/Node types, confirmed by grep to have zero std::fs/std::path/std::env/std::net usage -- compile against wasm32v1-none, the frozen-feature-set target that structurally cannot link std at all? Still expected-fail today for the same reason as every other cell: the crate root has no `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]` opt-out yet, and `serde`/`serde_json`/`thiserror` are pulled in with their default (std) feature sets, unconditionally, regardless of `io`/`engine`. Promote to expected-pass only once that opt-out lands and the unconditional deps are confirmed alloc-only-compatible -- at that point this cell passing is real evidence the algo/core split is genuinely host-independent, not merely feature-flagged, and a regression here specifically implicates something in algo/ or core/ picking up a hidden std or atomics dependency (see no-std-policy.json's sibling cells on the riscv32imc/riscv32imac pair for the atomics half of that story).
